title: 2010 HMMT February Calculus Problem 1
statement: Suppose that \(p(x)\) is a polynomial and that \(p(x)-p^{\prime}(x)=x^{2}+2 x+1\). Compute \(p(5)\).

solutions.text: 50 Observe that \(p(x)\) must be quadratic. Let \(p(x)=a x^{2}+b x+c\). Comparing coefficients gives \(a=1, b-2 a=2\), and \(c-b=1\). So \(b=4, c=5, p(x)=x^{2}+4 x+5\) and \(p(5)=25+20+5=50\).
